subject: black-spotted pond frog
title: A Hornet Sting Can Kill a Mouse. This Frog Eats Hornets Anyway

scenes.text: One hornet sting can kill a mouse. This frog eats hornets.
A scientist in Japan offered black-spotted pond frogs three kinds of hornet, giants included.
The frogs ate up to ninety-three percent of them. Even the giant, four times in five.
The hornets stung them in the mouth, sometimes in the eyes.
The frogs showed no visible harm. Nobody knows yet how they survive it.
People compare that sting to a hot nail. For this frog, it's lunch.

description:
In a 2025 study, black-spotted pond frogs ate 93% of yellow hornets (Vespa simillima), 87% of Vespa analis and 79% of northern giant hornets, despite being stung in the mouth and eyes.
A mouse of similar size can die from a single sting, but the frogs showed no noticeable harm. How they resist the venom is still an open question.
What other animal can shrug off a hornet?
first_comment: The largest frogs were matched with giant hornets almost two inches long. Would you rather face the frog or the hornet?
